audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer chart reads Skill on rows 1-3 and 5 (L1, L2, L3, L6) while content win[] and the packet chart both give Twisted Fate those rows — Kassadin is famously the weakest early laner and TF hard-wins pre-6.
audit.why: Content whys and packet levelChart agree; the full layer carries a generic survival template that fits assassins, not Kassadin's early game.
audit.corrected: phases[0], [1], [2], [4] sides moved to Twisted Fate with matching whys; win[] already correct so no content edits (no-ops avoided).

audit.why: Spikes are right: L3-5 is TF's kill window, 6 is the roam snowball, Rod/Rocketbelt is the hinge, late Kassadin un-1v1-able. suspectNames flags 'Gold Card' in spikes[0] — false positive, it is TF's real W card.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns has no digit and never mentions the Nether Blade (W) auto-reset burst tell flagged in missingInteractions; two Do's/Don'ts bullets are verbatim tradeGood/tradeBad bleed.
audit.why: Kit: Riftwalk 5/3.5/2s, Force Pulse 21-17s, Q shield absorbs magic damage (soaks Wild Cards). W auto-reset is his combo opener.
audit.corrected: Real cooldowns and the W wind-up tell written into breakdown.cooldowns; bleed bullets replaced with matchup-specific bodies.

edits.before: Kassadin wins by landing Riftwalk, denying your pattern, and turning your every misstep into the all-in you hadn’t budgeted.
edits.after: Kassadin wins by surviving your early lane, hitting Rod of Ages, and Riftwalking onto you faster than a gold card can answer.

edits.before: Q-farm from range and concede the duel question entirely — your level 1 is a wallet, not a weapon.
edits.after: Kassadin is one of the weakest level-1 laners in the game — you out-push and out-poke him instantly.

edits.before: W online: the gold card re-prices his every step-up. Lock yellow when he walks forward and the lane behaves.
edits.after: W online: with Wild Cards and a gold card you can genuinely all-in his feeble early game — walk him down.

edits.before: Full kit: stacked-deck autos plus card cycling is a real short trade — but your game is the clock, not the lane.
edits.after: Full kit: through level 3 you deny his CS and threaten kills he cannot answer — keep shoving into his tower.

edits.before: Destiny online — THE level in this lane. Every shove is now a bot-lane death sentence with a 130-second timer.
edits.after: Destiny online — roam and snowball the map while he is still a farming husk; every converted ult delays his spike.

edits.before: - Kassadin Riftwalk: matchup-defining — His mobility spike — the lane is decided before it scales. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W gold card has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Kassadin Riftwalk R: 5/3.5/2s per jump — never kite it, stun it. - His Nether Blade (W) auto-reset opens the combo; the wind-up is your step-back cue. - Your gold card has one job: the moment he jumps in. Your R: the moment his lane goes broke.

edits.before: Lock gold off-screen, walk up once, card-auto-Q, and leave — one stun-chunk per cycle is all the lane asks of you.
edits.after: Post-Rod, a freeze keeps you outside his 500-range Riftwalk threat while Wild Cards still collects from safety.

edits.before: Cycling cards inside his engage range for stacked-deck greed — TF dies in exactly one mistimed auto-walk per game; don't pre-book it.
edits.after: With gold card down, a 2-second Riftwalk puts him on top of you under tower — no plate is worth an assassin's reset window.

notes: Chart rows 0-2 and 4 moved to Twisted Fate on the full layer to agree with content win[] and the packet — content whys already argued the TF-favored early game and the full layer was a generic survival template. suspectNames 'Gold Card' in spikes[0] is a false positive (TF's real W card). missingInteractions autoreset-burst-tell folded into breakdown.cooldowns. His Q shield only absorbs MAGIC damage — worth noting it soaks Wild Cards poke specifically; content early already says to bait it. tldr/winCon keep a survival framing that fits post-Rod Kassadin but undersells the pre-6 kill window; content covers this correctly, left as-is to respect scope.
